result:
**Verdict: accept.**

Each blocker I raised is closed by the code as shown. I could not execute anything in this mode, so acceptance rests on the test run you report and on the pinned hash matching your tree.

- **Heuristic replaced with a positive contract.** The expected set is derived from every table introduction at or below the stored version, and the check runs before any pragma or DDL in both read-write and read-only opens. Missing expected tables and unexpected graph-prefixed tables are both rejected, so pure legacy v25 through v34 and the main-base plus legacy-tail hybrids all fail on at least two independent conditions. Main v25 through v27 pass because the upgrade tests open at exactly those versions with the check active.
- **Legacy DDL frozen.** The fixture's source commit is the current HEAD, and its ten migrations are pure creates, so the name-based check does not depend on legacy and integrated numbering lining up.
- **Main SQL pinned.** The hash over migrations 25 through 27, the contiguous id assertion, and the two name-to-id anchors will catch any drift at the integration boundary.
- **Read-only no longer converts journal mode.** The WAL pragma is now gated on read-write, and the read-only v27 test proves no graph DDL is applied. The crash test correctly asserts logical preservation rather than byte equality, since SQLite may checkpoint an abandoned WAL on close of the sole connection. The comment in db.ts documents that.
- **Rollback fault injection.** An index collision on a DB whose tables are all present passes the lineage check and then fails inside the migration transaction, so the transactional rollback path is still exercised as claimed.
- **Executor regression.** The clean-environment cancel test proves process-group exit with a fresh environment, and the explicit inheritEnv cases cover both directions. This assumes the process fixture invokes node by absolute path, since a clean environment has no usable PATH for a bare command name.

One non-blocking follow-up, directly on the new mechanism rather than on schema corruption: the regex-derived expected set is never compared against a schema the integrated build actually produced. No test in this file reopens a fully migrated database, so a graph table whose create statement the anchored, single-space regex fails to parse would reject every restart with no failing test here. A reopen-at-current test in both modes, plus loosening the regex whitespace to `\s+`, closes that in a few lines. Other suites that restart the daemon likely already cover reopen, so I am not holding acceptance on it.
